transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we proceed toward finalizing approval on the $30 million trade receivable securitization, I'd like to follow our standard pre-closing routine. Risk analyst and finance counsel — please report any transaction-specific issues you've identified so I can factor them into my decision. As a reminder, the key draft assumptions are: all $30 million of receivables treated as eligible, a 3% dilution reserve, ordinary seller support permitted, and a proposed funding date of November 20, 2026. Please walk me through anything that needs attention.

transcript.text: Maya, I need to flag a significant issue from my review of the October collections file, which I completed yesterday and is still in my working paper pending monthly risk-pack circulation. The file shows 6% historical dilution rather than the 3% assumed in the draft. Under our risk methodology, this requires an 8% dilution reserve. Additionally, $4,000,000 of the receivables are affiliate balances that must be excluded, leaving an eligible pool of exactly $26,000,000 — not $30,000,000 as the draft assumes.

transcript.text: Maya, I have a legal issue to flag. I received the transaction counsel memo this morning and have not yet attached it to the closing checklist. The memo confirms that the structure qualifies as a true sale only if two conditions are met: first, the seller has no recourse for ordinary obligor credit losses, and second, a UCC financing statement is perfected before the November 20, 2026 funding date. These are binding conditions that must be satisfied before funding, or the true sale characterization is at risk.
